additional_info.subject: RE: ID0388364-DC/Si-D/DE- [JT0Q0w] Charger Not Delivering 300kW CRM:00796000951
additional_info.body:
Hi Breilmann,
I hope this email finds you well.
We have analyzed the logs for the past day for all three chargers mentioned in the webform. Apart from one charger, there have been multiple successful charging sessions. We checked the logs for this specific charger (
jtIwGj
) over the past two days, but no charging sessions occurred. Below is the analysis we conducted in order to find the root cause.
The logs I’ve shared show that the EV functions as the Master and the charger functions as the Slave. The charger provided the current and voltage as demanded by the EV.
As you can see from the multiple session logs, the EV’s target current changed, and the EVSE current adjusted accordingly. EV charging operates on the principles of Constant Current (CC) and Constant Voltage (CV). Initially, the EV charges up to 80-85% SOC using CC, and then it gradually switches to CV mode based on the EV’s requirements. During this phase, the EV's target current drops to protect the battery from thermal runaway and to ensure proper cell balancing. You can refer to the blue and yellow highlighted values for Current and Voltage, respectively.
Charger:
CRFwcM
. Apart from these two long-duration sessions, there are multiple other sessions as well, but the result is the same in all of them.
Session_Start : 2024-11-06T11:28:57 Outlet2, EV SOC : 38%
Session_Start : 2024-11-06T12:50:13 Outlet1, EV SOC : 34%
Charger :
JT0Q0w
Session_Start ; 2024-11-06T13:58:52 Outlet2, EV SOC : 52%
One thing we noticed, along with the above, is that the power is being limited by the
ELMS
(External Load Management System) on both chargers.
In the charging session logs for both chargers, we observed the following values being sent by the
ELMS
:
[
ELM
] DC2 outlet power ELMS limit < CG.MaxPower Limit, PLimEvseSetpactive = 20 kW, PlimElmsOutlet = 17.6 kW, PlimCGmax = 140 kW
[
ELM
] DC1 outlet power ELMS limit < CG.MaxPower Limit, PLimEvseSetpactive = 20 kW, PlimElmsOutlet = 11.2 kW, PlimCGmax = 140 kW
Based on this analysis, we conclude that there is no issue with the EVSE. I hope this addresses your concerns
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Shrey
